open_obligations: Do not read Engels et al.'s flat debater Elo as contradicting Kenton et al.'s debater-strength effect without matching metrics.
Note Engels et al.'s very small question sets.
Check whether both use the same notion of debater strength (cross-play Elo versus general Elo).
in.other_title: In debate, judge (Guard) Elo rises with general intelligence while debater Elo stays flat
in.rationale: Kenton et al. report stronger debaters (higher Elo) yield higher judge accuracy on extractive tasks with a Gemini Pro 1.5 judge, but are less differentiated on closed tasks. Engels et al. report that across models spanning the Chatbot Arena range, debater domain Elo stays flat with general intelligence while judge Elo rises, on TruthfulQA, QuALITY and PrOntoQA with 20 questions per dataset; they vary judge and debater together and measure Elo, not accuracy.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: how debater and judge capability shape debate outcomes for LLMs

open_obligations: Check that Kenton et al.'s Elo-vs-accuracy result is positive for the extractive QA (reading comprehension) tasks specifically
Note that Kenton et al. vary strength via model size and best-of-N, while Arnesen et al. train Llama3-8B; compare judge strength across the two
Check whether this result also bears on Kenton et al.'s open question about training debaters (OPEN-TRAINING record)
in.other_title: Arnesen et al. report Kenton et al.'s positive debater-strength trend persists with debate training
in.rationale: This is an explicit claim that the authors' training result agrees with Kenton et al.'s inference-time result. Arnesen et al. note elsewhere (p10 L17-19, L30-32) that Kenton et al.'s positive findings were mainly for reading comprehension, which is the only domain tested here.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Debater strength vs judge accuracy; agreement is limited to reading comprehension, the only task Arnesen et al. test

open_obligations: Check whether the citing claim corresponds to Kenton et al.'s debater-Elo result or to their observation that stronger judge models are more accurate, which has no dedicated record
Check that the same Kenton et al. prompts and task types are used, so differences are not due to setup
in.other_title: Engels et al.'s debate judge scaling is consistent with Kenton et al.'s strength-accuracy findings
in.rationale: The authors explicitly state consistency with Kenton et al. Kenton et al. report that stronger debaters (by Elo) give marginally higher judge accuracy and that stronger judges are more accurate; the citing work measures judge and debater Elo across many models and finds judge gains but flat debater Elo.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether debate judge accuracy improves with stronger models in an information-asymmetric LLM-judge debate; holds for prompted, untrained models

open_obligations: Check whether the debater Elo ranges in the two tournaments are comparable.
Note Kenton et al. use 1-turn debates and a broader task set.
Check whether Kenton et al.'s QuALITY-only subset shows the Khan et al. trend.
out.other_title: Arguing the correct answer is easier, and the advantage grows with debater persuasiveness
out.rationale: Khan et al. report that the Elo advantage of being assigned the correct answer increases with aggregate Elo across 20 debaters judged by GPT-4-Turbo on QuALITY. Kenton et al. find a positive correct-answer Elo advantage for every debater but no clear trend of it growing with aggregate Elo, using 1-turn debates, different debater models and a Gemini Pro 1.5 judge across extractive and closed tasks.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether the advantage of arguing the correct answer grows with debater strength, in LLM debate cross-play tournaments

text: The paper reports that every debater has a positive Elo advantage when assigned the correct answer, but unlike Khan et al. (2024) there is no clear trend of this advantage growing with aggregate Elo. With Gemini Pro 1.5 judging, stronger debaters have higher Elo and yield higher judge accuracy on extractive tasks, while on closed tasks debaters are less differentiated in both Elo and judge accuracy.
title: Debater strength (Elo) vs judge accuracy and correct-answer advantage in debate
